text: Education in Sweden is structured into nine years of compulsory comprehensive school (grundskola), divided into three stages: lower (grades 1–3), middle (grades 4–6), and upper (grades 7–9). Students take 16 compulsory subjects across all stages, including Swedish, mathematics, physical education, English, and arts, with optional foreign language courses. From grade 6, students receive grades, and their total score (based on letter grades converted to numbers) is used for upper secondary school admissions. National tests are administered in grades 3, 6, and 9 to assess student progress. Upper secondary education (gymnasieskola) lasts three years and offers 18 national programs, including preparatory and vocational tracks. Students complete a diploma project and must pass 8–12 subjects depending on their program to qualify. Higher education includes university degrees (bachelor’s, master’s, PhD) and vocational training, with a strong emphasis on quality assurance and student support. Independent schools (friskolor) offer private, publicly funded education with diverse pedagogical approaches, though they face criticism over profit-making and grading practices. The system emphasizes equity, secularism, and student well-being, with a strong focus on inclusive and experiential learning.
